subject: Private Offer: multi-year prepay structure + ramp schedule for ClaraHealth
messages:
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Jennifer Park <jennifer.park@clarahealth.com>, Tom Ellis <t.ellis@clarahealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Aisha Rahman <aisha_rahman@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 24 Mar 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Private Offer: multi-year prepay structure + ramp schedule for ClaraHealth

Hi Jennifer / Tom —

Thanks again for the time yesterday. Per our discussion, attached is a draft term sheet outlining two options for ClaraHealth to consume Redwood via an AWS Marketplace private offer:

1) 3-year prepay with stepped ramp: 40% year 1 / 30% year 2 / 30% year 3; 22% list discount off hosted rates, with chargebacks if usage exceeds prepay in-year.
2) 1-year annual prepay (annual renewal) with a higher year-1 discount (18%) and a usage true-up at year-end.

Key questions we discussed: how ClaraHealth wants to structure the ramp (conservative vs. aggressive), whether the marketplace needs a single up-front invoice or annual invoices, and any rev-rec constraints on your side.

I've attached the Usage_Ramp_Template.xlsx to capture expected monthly token volumes by service and the AWS_PrivateOffer_Form.pdf for the marketplace intake. Vivek from finance is looped for amortization and revenue recognition questions.

Next steps: please confirm which option you prefer and any procurement constraints (PO cadence, billing contact, required SOW language). Happy to set a short call tomorrow to finalize inputs for the private offer.

Best,
Rishi
Director, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference

Attachments: Redwood_Term_Sheet_v3.pdf, Usage_Ramp_Template.xlsx, AWS_PrivateOffer_Form.pdf
From: Tom Ellis <t.ellis@clarahealth.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Cc: Jennifer Park <jennifer.park@clarahealth.com>, procurement-clarahealth@clarahealth.com
Date: Tue, 24 Mar 2026 11:04:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Private Offer: multi-year prepay structure + ramp schedule for ClaraHealth

Rishi —

Thanks for the term sheet. A few clarifications from procurement:  
- ClaraHealth prefers annual invoicing where possible (we cannot accept a single 3-year up-front invoice for CAPEX reasons). Would Redwood and AWS support an annual charge while still locking in a 3-year price?
- For the ramp: we expect heavy POC usage in Q2, then production kickoff in Q4. Can the year-1 prepay be sized lower with planned top-ups for predictable increases?
- We also need to confirm the discount stacks if we commit via Marketplace vs direct contract — procurement wants to ensure we're not losing enterprise concessions.

Can you provide a model that shows annual invoices with a 3-year price lock and the mechanics for mid-year top-ups?

Thanks,
Tom
Sr. Procurement Manager
ClaraHealth

Subject: Re: Private Offer: multi-year prepay structure + ramp schedule for ClaraHealth

Rishi — quick notes for the reply draft: 
- We can do a 3-year price lock while invoicing annually via AWS Marketplace private offers; AWS will still require the private offer form but supports annual invoicing schedules at the partner level (we've done this for one other customer).
- Offer a flexible top-up mechanism: allow ClaraHealth to purchase additional credits during the year at the contracted unit price (no penalty), with an end-of-year reconciliation. That satisfies procurement's need for lower initial capex.
- Discount stacking: clarify that marketplace fees ~5% are factored; we can match direct contract economics by folding the fee into the discount so ClaraHealth sees equivalent effective unit price. Leave the exact percent to finance to confirm.

I'll draft a short note to Amit at AWS to confirm the invoicing mechanics and the Private Offer acceptance timeline. Vivek — can you confirm the rev-rec / amortization implications for Redwood if we invoice annually against a 3-year price lock?

—Marissa
Sr. Account Exec, Redwood Inference
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>, Aisha Rahman <aisha_rahman@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 24 Mar 2026 16:08:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Private Offer: multi-year prepay structure + ramp schedule for ClaraHealth

Team —

Short answer on rev-rec: we can support a 3-year price lock with annual invoices, but Redwood must defer revenue recognition according to delivered consumption unless ClaraHealth signs a valid commitment and pays up-front. If they pay annually, we will recognize revenue as delivered (monthly). If the customer prefers to pay the full 3-year amount up-front but wants to amortize on their side, we can accept that but need clear cancellation clauses and refund mechanics for both parties.

Operational implications:
- Accounting prefers annual invoicing with committed MRR hints for forecasting.
- If we allow mid-year top-ups at the contracted rate, we need a process for generating amendment POs to the private offer so AWS billing matches the top-ups.

I'll provide a short blurb for Rishi to include in the procurement reply explaining our revenue recognition treatment and the amendment process.

—Vivek
Head of Finance, Redwood Inference
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Tom Ellis <t.ellis@clarahealth.com>, Jennifer Park <jennifer.park@clarahealth.com>, Amit Sinha <amit.sinha@amazon.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Aisha Rahman <aisha_rahman@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 25 Mar 2026 10:15:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Private Offer: multi-year prepay structure + ramp schedule for ClaraHealth

Tom / Jennifer / Amit —

Thanks for the quick turnaround. To summarize and propose a concrete structure that should meet procurement and accounting: 

Proposal (3-year price lock with annual invoicing + flexible top-ups)
- Contract term: 36 months with fixed unit pricing guaranteed for the term.
- Billing cadence: annual invoices (Year 1, Year 2, Year 3). Each invoice covers the committed prepay for that year.
- Year 1 prepay: 30% of contracted three-year spend to reduce initial outlay (captures POC to early-prod).
- Year 2: 35%. Year 3: 35%. (We can adjust to 40/30/30 if ClaraHealth prefers more aggressive front-load.)
- Top-ups: ClaraHealth may purchase additional credits any time at the contracted unit price; we will process an amendment to the private offer so AWS billing aligns.
- Reconciliation: year-end reconciliation/true-up for usage above prepay; any overage billed at contracted rates.

Vivek from finance will be the point for rev-rec language. Amit — can you confirm AWS Marketplace mechanics for annual invoicing with private offers and amendment handling? Our preference is that AWS issues annual invoices that Redwood receives and then passes through to ClaraHealth (standard private offer flow).

If this looks good, Tom/Jennifer can confirm and we will produce a final private offer submission (I attached the updated term sheet).

Best,
Rishi
Director, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference

Attachments: Redwood_Term_Sheet_v3.pdf
From: Amit Sinha <amit.sinha@amazon.com>

Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 25 Mar 2026 12:34:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Private Offer: multi-year prepay structure + ramp schedule for ClaraHealth

Rishi / Tom / Jennifer —

Confirming AWS can support a Private Offer with a 3-year price lock and annual billing schedule. A few operational notes: 
- AWS requires the Private Offer form completed with annual invoice cadence selected; Redwood must be listed as the seller of record for pass-through billing.
- Mid-term top-ups are supported via amendments; each amendment creates a line item and will generate a separate invoice for the incremental purchase.
- Marketplace fees are assessed on each invoice; typically ~4.5%. If Redwood wants to guarantee net pricing to ClaraHealth, you should include margin to account for that fee in the private offer price.
- Timeline: once we receive the completed AWS_PrivateOffer_Form.pdf and legal sign-off, standard processing is ~7-10 business days. Expedited reviews possible but require AWS Marketplace PM approval.

I'll accept the form and open the intake once Redwood submits. Happy to jump on a short call tomorrow to walk procurement through the mechanism.

Regards,
Amit Sinha
Sr. Partner Lead, AWS Marketplace
From: Jennifer Park <jennifer.park@clarahealth.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>, Amit Sinha <amit.sinha@amazon.com>

Date: Thu, 26 Mar 2026 15:48:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Private Offer: multi-year prepay structure + ramp schedule for ClaraHealth

Rishi / Amit —

This structure looks acceptable to ClaraHealth. We will: 
1) Proceed with a 3-year price lock with annual invoices (30/35/35 split).
2) Use mid-year top-ups as needed; procurement will submit amendment POs for top-ups.
3) Please submit the AWS_PrivateOffer_Form.pdf and the final term sheet; legal will review the private offer and return redlines (expect ~5 business days).

Thanks for accommodating the annual invoice request — that resolves our CAPEX constraint. Tom and procurement will expect the official private offer packet by end of day Friday so we can route internally.

Best,
Jennifer Park
Head of Cloud Integrations, ClaraHealth
